name: Basalt Errata
description: Basalt Errata is a rocky world whose geological record is full of contradictions. Mountain ranges of dark basalt rise from plains of lighter sedimentary rock that should not exist on a world this dry, and dried ocean basins contain mineral deposits consistent with warm, saline water despite temperature records suggesting the planet has been frozen for millions of years. Crystal caverns beneath the mountain ranges hold formations that grow in defiance of the ambient conditions, incorporating water that has no identified source.

The thin atmosphere supports little weather, but occasional dust storms sweep across the dried basins, revealing and concealing the erroneously placed geological features in cycles that frustrate systematic mapping. The light has a grey, overcast quality filtered through high-altitude dust, and the temperature hovers near freezing during the day before dropping sharply at night. Microbial life thrives in the crystal caverns, sustained by the mysterious water source and chemical energy from the mineral formations.

A freighter, the cargo vessel Misprint, crash-landed here six decades ago after a navigation error brought it out of transit in the wrong system entirely. The crew survived and were eventually rescued, but the ship remains embedded in a basalt ridge, its hull breached and its cargo—industrial chemicals intended for a terraforming operation—slowly leaching into the surrounding rock. The chemicals have reacted with the native minerals in unexpected ways, creating new crystal formations that grow at visible rates.

Geologists consider Basalt Errata a world of errors—a planet whose geology consistently contradicts the conditions that should govern it. The leading theory is that the planet underwent a rapid and recent transformation from oceanic to arid conditions, possibly within the last hundred thousand years, but the mechanism remains unknown. The crash site's chemical contamination has inadvertently created a natural experiment in accelerated mineral formation that may help explain the planet's contradictory features. Every answer found here seems to generate two new questions.
